cand.title: 2027 Atwood Colloquium
cand.organizationName: University of Toronto Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: No verified 2027 hotel buyer or contracting authority was identified. Michelle Su is named Atwood Chair and Dan Yang and May Jagodkin are named co-chairs on the 2026 programme page; these are historical event-organizer roles, not verified 2027 appointments. Dan Yang is also a verified 2026–27 EGSA co-president. Petra Dreiser, Communications & Outreach Coordinator, and Mihai Baetu, Chief Administrative Officer, are departmental routing contacts; their roles do not establish hotel contract control.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced for April 29–30, 2027, 9:00 am–6:00 pm, at Koffler House, 569 Spadina Crescent, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. These are activity dates from Event Details, not publication dates, and fall within the requested horizon. No official 2028 edition announcement was located; do not extrapolate dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: potential fit is short-stay lodging for invited speakers or other non-local academic visitors, not exclusive accommodation for the colloquium. The official audience is students, postdocs and faculty from the three U of T campuses and ROM, plus three guest speakers; participant count must not be treated as travelling room demand. Overnight need could be small and is unquantified; there is no evidence for a 15–109 peak-room group, extended stays or relocation. The 157-room Harbourfront hotel is not the campus venue, and its MTCC proximity does not create an event-specific advantage here. City-hotel visitor lodging is more plausible than resort use. Main meetings are already assigned to Koffler House; no off-site meeting, reception or catering demand is established, and hotel restaurant/lounge availability must be verified separately.
findings.venueCommitments: The 2027 official listing states “Location: Koffler House, 569 Spadina Crescent.” This is a published university venue commitment, not evidence of a signed contract or hotel booking. It is in Toronto proper, at the St. George campus in downtown Toronto, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The specific 2027 room is not published. Do not confuse this building with Koffler Scientific Reserve.
findings.historicalRotation: 2023: April 26–27, Koffler House, KP108; 2024: April 24–25, Koffler House; 2025: April 10–11 per official event listing, Koffler House; 2026: April 23–24, Koffler House, 569 Spadina Crescent. Together with the announced 2027 venue, this supports repeat campus hosting rather than destination or hotel rotation. The 2025 PDF cover renders April 10–12, conflicting with the official event listing; its detailed sessions are headed April 10 and April 11. Preserve that historical discrepancy.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. The 2027 page states “In addition to our own biologists, three guest speakers round out the cutting-edge program each year,” but contains no lodging instructions. No edition-specific host hotel, room block, official housing bureau, hotel names, open RFP or accommodation procurement contact was located in the reviewed event pages/programmes. There is therefore no accommodation-sourcing statement to quote. This is an evidence gap, not proof that sourcing is open or that no private arrangements exist. Graduate student housing advice is not an Atwood hotel commitment.
findings.organizationStructure: University academic department event, not a commercial association congress or corporate relocation programme. The department publishes the event; graduate students select the Atwood Lecturer and the lecture series is supported by an Atwood-family endowment. The published programme identifies an internal chair, co-chairs and organizing committee. No external PCO, DMC, agency or housing bureau was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No incumbent hotel, sold-out block, compression or overflow evidence was found. The verified limitation is that the meeting venue is already assigned to Koffler House. Inference: campus access and potentially limited non-local attendance weaken a Harbourfront lodging pitch; no specific competing hotel can be named as committed. A participant profile reports approximately 200 attendees historically, but does not establish overnight demand or 2027 attendance.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Petra Dreiser through her published departmental address and ask for the 2027 Atwood lead and person arranging invited-speaker accommodation. Reference Dan Yang’s 2026 organizing role and 2026–27 EGSA co-presidency as an introduction path; Michelle Su is an additional historical organizer. Ask whether lodging is centrally booked, already committed or individually arranged; obtain guest count, arrival/departure dates, existing hotel arrangements, budget and payment process. Only if uncommitted non-local demand exists, offer a small flexible visitor-room proposal for the April 29–30 event with stay dates determined by travel plans. Do not quote a room block, catering package or extended-stay requirement before confirmation.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: The 2027 edition is confirmed upcoming and its meeting location is published. Hotel sourcing remains unconfirmed, not open. A conditional speaker-lodging conversation is reasonable; a live room-block opportunity or main-meeting bid is not established. The 2026 edition is past and is used only as historical evidence.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Verified annual recurrence supports relationship development, but not an open future tender or destination rotation. Inference: seek consideration for recurring invited-speaker stays while retaining campus meetings; do not sell venue displacement or a future hotel block as confirmed. No announced 2028 dates, venue or housing decision was located.
